components.name: Scripture + Notes (Paracol)
components.description: Core content layout: 48/52 split, scripture left (Latin Modern Roman), pastor's notes right (All Round Gothic).
components.html:
11 For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation for all people, 12 training us to renounce ungodliness and worldly passions, and to live self-controlled, upright, and godly lives in the present age...

Grace is the subject — the active agent. Not our response to grace, but grace itself as teacher.

"Appeared" (ἐπεφάνη) — epiphany. A technical term for divine manifestation.

narrative.overview:
This is a document in the tradition of scholarly scriptural apparatus: clean hierarchical typography, structured pages that feel composed rather than generated, and a purple that functions as ink rather than brand accent. Every page is a unit of attention — the reader comes to study, not scan, and the layout honors that. The right-side lavender rule echoes the column ruling of medieval manuscripts, here serving as both a visual anchor and a gentle reminder that this margin is workspace.

The system uses four distinct font families, each assigned a single semantic role with no overlap: rounded gothic for the pastor's voice, classical roman for scripture, geometric sans for structure and navigation, and a script for the human byline. Helvetica Neue stands apart for commentary — a deliberate sans-serif signal that this is not the pastor's voice. The document is typeset for the Remarkable Paper Pro (A5, 229 PPI, e-ink), where no color reaches the reader except as a grayscale value.

This system explicitly rejects: church bulletin aesthetic; generic PDF template look; PowerPoint handout style; modern SaaS-clean minimalism; study Bible populism with colored call-out boxes and rounded-rectangle sidebars.
keyCharacteristics: Four-register font system: each family has one semantic role, never shared
Page-as-unit composition: each sub-point owns a page, each page feels resolved
Purple as scholarly ink: structural, never decorative
Flat on e-ink: hierarchy through weight and scale only, no shadows
Annotation-first margins: the outer margin is workspace, not padding

rules.name: The Single Ink Rule
rules.body: Scholiast Purple and Rubric Red appear only in structural roles: links, navigation, and heading-level rubrication. They are never used for emphasis within body text, callouts, or decorative borders. Their rarity is what makes them readable as navigational signals on a grayscale screen.

rules.name: The Grayscale Contract
rules.body: Every color decision must survive a grayscale rendering. The primary differentiator on e-ink is not hue but luminance. Design for luminance values, not RGB hues.

rules.name: The Four-Register Rule
rules.body: Each font family is assigned one semantic category and never appears outside it: All Round Gothic = pastor's voice; Latin Modern Roman = scripture; Josefin Sans = structure/navigation; Helvetica Neue = external commentary.

rules.name: The Size-Step Rule
rules.body: Scripture and commentary are set at \small (approx. 9pt) against the \normalsize (approx. 10pt) body. This 1pt step combined with font-family contrast is sufficient to signal register change. Do not increase scripture size to match the body.

rules.name: The Flat-and-Final Rule
rules.body: If a layout problem seems to call for a box, border, background tint, or shadow, the correct answer is almost always a typographic solution instead: a weight increase, a font switch, a page break, or additional vertical space.

dos: Do set the speaker name in the script cascade — it is the only expressive typographic gesture and earns its place by making the document personal.
Do use \vfill to distribute vertical space on the title page. Fixed \vspace values cause overflow when a cover image is present.
Do cap cover images at width=0.75\textwidth, height=0.38\textheight, keepaspectratio. The title page must never overflow.
Do start each section on a new page. The section break is structural, not optional.
Do use the 48/52 paracol split for scripture/notes, not 50/50. The asymmetry signals which column is anchor.
Do test every color and spacing decision against its grayscale rendering.
donts: Don't use clip art, borders, drop shadows, background color fills, or decorative elements anywhere in the document.
Don't use Times New Roman 12pt with 1-inch margins and no hierarchy.
Don't use bullet-heavy layouts with large fonts sized for projection.
Don't add colored call-out boxes, pull quotes in rounded rectangles, or sidebars.
Don't mix font-family roles. Each family has exactly one semantic category.
Don't use the body font for scripture quotations. The font switch is the hierarchy.
Don't use thin fonts, excessive whitespace, or cold neutral grays.
Don't use any design pattern that depends on color distinction to function on e-ink.
